Title: Private credit's calm carries a lagging shadow

Rating: underweight

The tape offers little to argue with on its face: a quiet session, prints in line, spreads holding at 400bps, and a headline drawdown of +0.0%.¹ Calder & Root read this as vindication — policy support resolving stress, the cycle staying the course. We read the same absence of movement as the more interesting datum. Private credit marks do not move on quiet sessions; they move on revaluation events, and revaluation events are precisely what a 5.00% policy rate held this long is designed to postpone rather than prevent.

Consider the gap between reported and public-market proxies, at -0.2% — narrow, almost reassuring. But narrow gaps in this asset class tend to widen discontinuously rather than drift, since marks are set by committees with quarterly memories, not by continuous auction.² The one-year return of +11.0% against a year-to-date figure of +1.1% is the chart worth describing rather than plotting: a steep, smooth ascent through most of the trailing year that has gone essentially flat in the most recent stretch — not reversed, not accelerated, just becalmed at a rate (5.00%) that keeps refinancing arithmetic tight for the borrowers underlying these books. Flat is not the same as resolved.

CPI at 2.9% gives the Committee room to talk about "support" without committing to cuts large enough to actually loosen credit conditions for the marginal borrower. Calder & Root's stay-the-course thesis assumes the policy path does the deleveraging work quietly, off-screen. Our prior says fragility compounds precisely off-screen, in vintages not yet marked to the stress they already contain.

Risk to this view: if the rate path eases meaningfully from 5.00% before the next marking cycle, the lag we're pricing in simply never materializes as loss, and this note ages as unnecessarily dour.

¹ Zero is a mark, not an observation.
² A committee's silence is not liquidity.
